# Sending Pictures and Files to Customers

OrderHub lets you send a customer a screenshot, photo or PDF while you're messaging them by text (SMS) or email. Use it to send a proof, a photo of a damaged print, a screenshot of their order or an invoice, without leaving OrderHub.

This article explains what the customer receives and how replies work. A separate article covers setting it up.



---

## Where you can send from

You can attach files wherever you message a customer in OrderHub:

* **On an order**, in the order's Messages panel.
* **On a customer's record**, in their Messages card. You can use this even if the customer has never texted you.

Press the paperclip (**Attach picture or file**) and choose up to **5 files**, each up to **10 MB**. Add a message if you want, pick **SMS**, **Email** or **Both**, and send.

* Note: large photos are made smaller automatically before sending, so they go through quickly and arrive clearly.



---

## What the customer receives

How a file arrives depends on where the customer is and what the file is.

| What you send | How it arrives |
| --- | --- |
| A picture (JPEG, PNG or GIF) texted to a **US or Canadian mobile** | As a real picture inside the text message |
| A picture texted to a **UK or other international** number | As a short link in the text |
| A **PDF** or other document, by text | As a short link in the text |
| A **second or later** picture in the same text | As a short link in the text |
| Any file sent by **email** | As a short link in the email |

* Note: real picture messages only work in the US and Canada, and only once your lab has been moved to OrderHub's newer texting system. Until then, pictures arrive as links.

### What a link looks like

Links are short and show your brand's name, for example:

**media.pixfizz.com/yourbrand/f/8Kd2xQp**

If your brand has its own download web address, the link uses that instead.

When the customer taps the link, a simple page opens with your brand name, the picture or PDF, and a **Download** button. They don't need an app, account or password.



### Links expire after 30 days

Every link stops working after **30 days**, so private photos and invoices aren't left open online. After that, the customer sees *"This link has expired. Please ask us to send the file again."*

The file stays in the conversation in OrderHub, so you can simply send it again and a new link is made.

---

## Choosing the brand for a link

A link always shows a brand, so the customer knows who it's from:

* **Sending from an order:** the order's brand is used.
* **Sending from a customer's record, or from an order with no brand:** OrderHub asks **"Which brand is this file from?"** You must pick one before you can send.
* **Labs with only one brand:** that brand is used automatically, and you're never asked.



---

## When the customer replies

* **By text:** the reply appears in the same conversation in OrderHub. If they text you a picture, it's saved and shown in the conversation too.
* **By email:** replies go to your brand's reply-to mailbox, not into OrderHub. Look for them there.

* Note: you only see a picture a customer texts in once your lab is on OrderHub's newer texting system.

---

## Good to know

* Up to 5 files per message, 10 MB each.
* Send PDFs as links. Phones show PDFs in picture messages badly, so OrderHub always sends them as links.
* Anyone with a link can open it until it expires, just like a Dropbox or WeTransfer link. Links are practically impossible to guess.
* Files you send and receive stay visible to staff in the conversation. Only the customer's link expires.
